title: Process drift — 4 sprint PRs in a row merged without sprint label or sprint JSON
summary: Systemic workflow regression — PRs #227 (S177), #228 (S178), #229 (S179), #230 (S180) all merged into main without either (a) the `sprint` GitHub label, or (b) a `backlog/sprints/S<NN>.sprint.json` file. Visible symptoms: `engine:doctor` Backlog section can't see them (no sprint JSON); `npm run qa:next-pr` won't surface them as unreviewed (no `sprint` label means `gh pr list --label sprint --state merged` skips them); the dogfooded QA workflow effectively goes dark for ~24 h after S176. Same pattern previously hit once with S158 (PR #198, addressed by promoting QA-2026-05-27-001 + adding the missing JSON in PR #200) — that was treated as a one-off then. Four-in-a-row promotes it to a process regression worth fixing in the convention enforcement layer, not just one ticket per gap. CLAUDE.md §Working Mode states 'always pass --label sprint' and §QA-Workflow points at the canonical `gh pr create --base main --label sprint --title "S<NN>: ..."` recipe; CI / preflight currently does NOT verify that the merged sprint PR (a) carries the label, or (b) shipped a sprint JSON. Both checks are mechanical and would catch the drift.
repro: From origin/main HEAD `d9e6c35` run `git ls-tree origin/main backlog/sprints/ | grep -E 'S17[7-9]|S180'` — returns nothing. S150-S176 are all present; S177-S180 absent.
Run `gh pr list --label sprint --state merged --limit 10` — last sprint-labelled PR is #226 (S176). #227-#230 are not in that list.
Run `for pr in 227 228 229 230; do gh pr view $pr --json labels --jq '[.labels[].name] | join(",")'; done` — empty string for each. No labels at all.
Confirm the work itself shipped: `git log --oneline origin/main | head` shows S177-S180 commits + the source/test changes are on main, only the meta (label + JSON) is missing.

Confirm tooling effects: `npm run qa:next-pr` won't see these as candidate sprints to review; `npm run engine:doctor -- examples/kaboom-crew` Backlog section's recent-commits list shows the PRs but the sprint-status block can't enumerate them as archived sprints with stories.
expected: Every sprint PR merging into main carries both (a) the `sprint` label, and (b) a committed `backlog/sprints/S<NN>.sprint.json` file. Either CI rejects PRs that violate the convention OR the dev's PR-open helper writes both automatically. The four-in-a-row drift suggests a manual recipe that's easy to forget — automation closes the gap.
actual: PRs #227, #228, #229, #230 merged without labels or sprint JSONs. The QA agent can't see them via the canonical `qa:next-pr` path; the dogfood backlog views in `engine:doctor` are blind to the work. Each sprint individually shipped fine (suite 2027/2027 green) — only the meta tracking is broken.
logs:
Pattern of missing sprints (no JSON on main):
  S177 — PR #227 — heightmap visual pillars
  S178 — PR #228 — bomber HeightLift
  S179 — PR #229 — ramps via heightmap
  S180 — PR #230 — shadows-on castShadow defaults

PR label state (all four):
  gh pr view 227 --json labels --jq '[.labels[].name] | join(",")' → ""
  gh pr view 228 ... → ""
  gh pr view 229 ... → ""
  gh pr view 230 ... → ""

Fix outlines:
  1. **CI guard** — add a sprint-PR-shape job to `.github/workflows/`: when a PR's title matches `^S\d+:` or `^S\d+ ` and the diff touches backlog/, fail unless (a) `sprint` label is present AND (b) `backlog/sprints/S<NN>.sprint.json` is in the diff. Mirrors the qa-intake-auto-merge file-path gate but in the OTHER direction.
  2. **Dev-side helper** — the dev terminal opens sprint PRs via `gh pr create`. Extend the canonical recipe in CLAUDE.md (§Working Mode) so the helper script writes the sprint JSON + adds the label as one step. A small `scripts/backlog/sprint-open.mjs` that wraps `gh pr create` and asserts the JSON exists before opening would catch this at the source.
  3. **Post-hoc heal** — when the QA terminal notices a sprint PR without a JSON, file the JSON ourselves (as the QA agent did for S158 in PR #200). Reactive only — keeps the workflow visible but doesn't prevent the next drift.

Variant 1 is the proper long-term fix; Variant 2 is preventative; Variant 3 is the band-aid we've been doing.

Also worth: when the JSONs are added retroactively, include them in a single small PR labelled `sprint-meta-backfill` so the change set is obvious in archival history.
